nodes.label: MathUp (Hebrew RTL bagrut math-5 study platform)
nodes.rationale: Evolved from an AI-question generator into a static-first learning platform because hand-authored verified content renders at zero API cost; AI became the fallback, not the engine.

nodes.label: Build + typecheck before every push
nodes.rationale: Push to main auto-deploys and the owner only ever views the live site, so an edit is not done until pushed. Vercel Hobby runtime differs from next dev; deploys that passed local typecheck have failed in prod and cost money.

nodes.label: Pathspec-only git commits (never git add . / -A)
nodes.rationale: The repo carries parallel work-in-progress (statistics.ts, 2020-summer-582.ts, untracked dirs); a blanket stage would sweep in-flight edits into an unrelated commit.

nodes.label: Vercel Hobby 60s serverless cap (maxDuration = 60)
nodes.rationale: Every model call must be paired with a max_tokens that fits inside 60s, otherwise the route returns nothing and still bills Anthropic — paying for a timed-out response.

nodes.label: ~$5/month Anthropic budget ceiling
nodes.rationale: Budget is tiny, so model ping-pong during bug hunts is forbidden and the $0 static-first / cache paths are preferred over any API call.

nodes.label: Prompt caching on large static system prompts (cache_control: ephemeral)
nodes.rationale: Large invariant system prompts are the cheapest thing to cache, and caching them is the main lever keeping grounded Sonnet chat inside the monthly budget.

nodes.label: Never put Hebrew inside KaTeX
nodes.rationale: KaTeX implements no bidi algorithm, so Hebrew inside $...$ renders reversed. Hebrew goes outside the math; subscripts use Latin letters ($m_1$, never $m_{משיק}$).

nodes.label: 5-unit bagrut math conventions (cis degrees, y²=2px, c²=a²−b²)
nodes.rationale: The Israeli MOE syllabus uses the y²=2px parabola with focus (p/2,0), not the American 4px form, and complex numbers in cis/degrees rather than e^{iθ}. Using American conventions would teach students notation the examiner does not accept.

nodes.label: Trigonometry degrees/radians split (owner decision 2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: trig-equations and special-angles-reduction are in degrees; trig-calculus must stay in radians because (sin x)' = cos x only holds in radians (in degrees it is (π/180)·cos x). Over-generalizing the complex-numbers 'degrees' rule to all trig once produced a wrong instruction. Guarded by scripts/verify-trig-angles.ts; verify-trig.ts hardcodes its own math and never reads content, so it cannot catch a convention regression.

nodes.label: IP boundary — no publisher solution books
nodes.rationale: Publisher solutions (יואל גבע, m-math.co.il, publisher PDFs) are copyrighted even when freely downloadable. Only MOE bagrut question text (public domain), the MOE syllabus, the model's own knowledge, and the owner's handwritten solutions are valid sources.

nodes.label: Only two question types exist (MCQ + open)
nodes.rationale: The owner already evaluated and rejected drag-drop, fill-blank, match and speed-drill formats; depth comes from adding more of the two accepted types, not from inventing new interaction models.

nodes.label: "Premium white" light-only design system
nodes.rationale: App is deliberately light-only with no dark-mode toggle: ivory canvas, indigo primary, gold reserved for achievements. Source of truth is app/globals.css :root, so new UI composes Tailwind plus the named utilities instead of inventing colors.

nodes.label: Dark-ink-on-light SVG diagram palette + custom-SVG-only rule
nodes.rationale: Light-on-dark stroke values are literally invisible on the ivory canvas. Diagrams must be type:'custom' raw SVG and never fn: closures, because a function crosses the RSC server→client boundary and crashes the page.

nodes.label: Monetization: free base, Pro depth (lib/access.ts)
nodes.rationale: Guided lessons and drills are static and cost $0 to serve, so they are the growth hook and must never be gated; only the Pro-depth surfaces (advanced course, archive, unlimited chat, AI photo-solve, advanced analytics) are paywalled. canAccessTopic no longer paywalls topics — topicLockReason is now purely pedagogical. There is no real billing yet: isProUser = ADMIN_EMAIL or an unset user_metadata.pro flag.

nodes.label: Static-first content architecture (zero API cost)
nodes.rationale: ~829 hand-authored, mathematically-verified questions live as TypeScript modules under content/ and render with no API call at all, which is what makes the free tier sustainable on a $5/month budget.

nodes.label: concept-quiz registry keyed `${subject}:${topic}`
nodes.rationale: Keying on topic alone is unsafe because math4 shares math5's Hebrew topic names and not always byte-identically; the composite subject:topic key makes adding a new subject one registry line.

nodes.label: Photo-scan caching: answer library first, AI last
nodes.rationale: /api/solve-photo runs cheap Sonnet-vision transcription, then matchQuestion (exact hash + Jaccard ≥0.82 over all static questions, free), then the Supabase solution_cache (free); only a true miss pays for AI text-solve, whose result is written back to the cache so the same question is never paid for twice.

nodes.label: localStorage-only client state (works without login, $0)
nodes.rationale: Keeping results, study plan, progress, adaptive difficulty and scans in localStorage means the product works for anonymous visitors and costs nothing to store.

nodes.label: lib/answer-check.ts deterministic mathjs grading
nodes.rationale: Grading open answers deterministically instead of via AI keeps them free. Gotchas: mathjs `log` IS natural log (write expected as log(2), not ln(2)), and trig evaluates in radians, so trig `expected` must be plain numbers/degrees or {kind:'manual'}.

nodes.label: npm run verify:content (scripts/verify-content.ts)
nodes.rationale: Supersedes check-katex-hebrew.ts because it imports the content modules instead of grepping source, so it can scope rules per field — '$= 4 - 3i$' is fine in solution.steps and a defect in keyPoints. Errors: hebrew-in-math, unbalanced $, $$display$$ mid-prose-line.

nodes.label: npm run verify:concept (shape-only gate + inventory table)
nodes.rationale: Checks SHAPE only and says so in its header — every `correct` index still has to be re-derived by hand, independently of whoever authored it. PROMOTED_TO_ERROR stays false until the 252-question target is met, because a gate that always fails gets bypassed within a day.

nodes.label: verify-mcq-distinct coverage honesty ("0 problems" ≠ correct)
nodes.rationale: It skips any option containing =, <, > or Hebrew (correct — those are statements, not values), which leaves 39% coverage on the concept bank and 0% on אלגברה. It now prints per-topic coverage and names every unchecked question, and that list IS the manual-review worklist. '0 problems' means 'nothing I examined failed', not 'the data is correct'.

nodes.label: MathText single-element contract (2026-07-28)
nodes.rationale: Both modes return exactly one element (span.mathtext-inline / div.mathtext-block), each dir="rtl". Inline mode used to return a bare fragment, which let a display:flex caller turn every word and formula into its own flex item (the 'לזכור' box rendered as 3 scrambled columns). dir must be "rtl" not "auto", because KaTeX emits raw LaTeX in a clip-hidden <annotation> and auto-detection reads a Latin first-strong char, flipping Hebrew lines that open with math. Left-alignment of standalone equations is driven by a .math-only class computed from the source string, since :only-child ignores text nodes.

nodes.label: The deliberate unscoped .katex floor in globals.css
nodes.rationale: Every scoped bidi rule needs a .chat-md/.math-content ancestor, so a MathText rendered without one inherited direction:rtl from <html dir="rtl"> and showed the formula reversed. 4 of 12 call sites in /quiz had no wrapper — all in the end-of-quiz mistake review, where students read their own wrong answers backwards. The floor is intentionally soft (two declarations, no !important) so the scoped block still wins; it only removes the failure mode where nothing applies. Do not 'clean up' the apparent duplicate.

nodes.label: Deliberate model routing (Sonnet grounded / Haiku generic)
nodes.rationale: /api/chat uses claude-sonnet-4-6 (prompt-cached) for grounded topics and claude-haiku-4-5 for generic; TUTOR_SONNET_TOPICS is a cost valve that demotes topics to Haiku if spend climbs. solve-photo needs Sonnet vision because Hebrew+LaTeX transcription is beyond Haiku. Micro-endpoints run Haiku. Question-generation routes survive only as a legacy fallback for subjects without a static bank.

nodes.label: Supabase tables created in dashboard; code degrades gracefully
nodes.rationale: Tables are created via SQL in the dashboard rather than git migrations, so a feature can ship before its table exists. Every call site wraps in try/catch and no-ops, and RLS is enforced everywhere. The owner must run the SQL before a new table's feature works live.

nodes.label: PROTECTED_PREFIXES middleware and the public /practice, /roadmap surfaces
nodes.rationale: /pricing, /roadmap and /practice stay public so an anonymous visitor following an old link never hits a login wall. That also makes /roadmap and /practice the only surfaces usable to verify shared rendering without a login — /quiz cannot be checked that way.

nodes.label: Strict CSP in next.config.ts (self + *.supabase.co)
nodes.rationale: Adding any external service (payment provider, Resend, etc.) requires updating connect-src/script-src or it silently breaks in production while working locally.

nodes.label: Bulk authoring: one agent per file, verify independently
nodes.rationale: Topics live in separate files so one agent per file avoids write conflicts; an authoring agent's own verification is circular, so the real checker must be re-run independently afterward.
